context.q: How do I cut music on the beat?
context.a: Press M while playing to drop markers on the beats (`markers.add`), turn on Snap (`sequence.snap`) and cut to the markers; fit the song to the length with Remix (`clip.remix`).

q: ok done, but now every cut lands on a beat and it feels boring
a: Cutting on every beat is monotonous: cut on phrases and accents instead.

context.q: How do I cut on action?
context.a: Find the same moment of the movement in both angles and cut a few frames into it; fine-tune with the Rolling Edit tool (`tool.rolling`).

q: how do I nudge it a frame at a time?
a: Roll the edit with `trim.edit` (roll type) and step it with `trim.forward` / `trim.backward`, a frame at a time, until the motion carries across the cut.

context.q: How do I keep versions, not one ever-changing sequence?
context.a: Duplicate the sequence (`edit.duplicate` in the Project panel) and keep working on the copy.

q: and what about crashes, do versions cover that?
a: No, auto-saves and the journal cover crashes: the journal recovers unsaved changes (`file.recover`). Versions cover "the old one was better".

context.q: Set up a music bed under my narration
context.a: Put Ducking on the music clip (`essentialSound.generateDucking`) so it sits roughly 15–20 dB under the voice while words play, or ride the music fader in Touch mode.

context.q: the music jumps up in every tiny pause
context.a: That's pumping: slow the fades or lower the ducking sensitivity.

q: should I just fix the levels with a limiter on the mix?
a: No: using the limiter to make things fit squashes the mix. Set the levels first, then a Hard Limiter on the Mix strip (`mixer.addInsert`) at −1 dB only holds the peaks.

context.q: How do I high-pass every voice?
context.a: Reduce Rumble in Essential Sound (3–4 = 66–78 Hz) or a High Pass effect.

q: there's still one loud p pop in the voiceover
a: Don't push the high-pass up for one pop, that thins the whole voice. Dip the Volume with a quick keyframe on that pop (Effect Controls), or cut it out under room tone.

context.q: How do I make a vertical version of my edit?
context.a: Duplicate the sequence (`edit.duplicate`), set it to 1080 × 1920 or 2160 × 3840 (`sequence.settings`) and reposition each clip with Motion ▸ Position.

q: the speaker walks around, do I keyframe the position the whole way?
a: Automatic reframing isn't offered yet; tracking can make the crop follow the subject (see tracking), otherwise keyframe Position where they move.

context.a: Export ▸ Captions… (`captions.export`) as SRT or WebVTT, delivered next to the video.

a: Burn them in for autoplaying social clips: captions from the transcript with short single lines, styled big with a stroke (`captions.setStyle`), burned in at export and kept in the middle third, away from the buttons.

context.q: Make my title slide in from the left
context.a: Keyframe Position at the start of the graphic and set the keyframes to Ease In / Ease Out (`effects.setInterpolation`) so it slows into place.

q: nice, and how should it leave?
a: The same way it came in: keyframe Position or Opacity at the end too, so it doesn't pop off. Protect both ends with responsive time (`graphics.setResponsiveTime`) so trims keep the animation.

context.q: How do I add the same channel logo to all my videos?
context.a: Make it once and Upgrade to Source Graphic (`graphics.upgradeToSourceGraphic`) so every use updates together.

q: it changes colour slightly under my graded shots
a: Graphics shouldn't go through the creative grade: keep the logo on a track above the graded clips, and no adjustment layer with a look above it.

context.q: What's the usual order of work on a film?
context.a: Assembly (everything in script order) → rough cut (structure, the right takes) → fine cut (timing, trims, sound edits) → picture lock.

context.q: how do I keep the earlier passes?
context.a: One sequence per pass: duplicate it in the Project panel (`edit.duplicate`) and name it by date or version.

q: and the sound while all that happens?
a: Rough levels only while cutting: Essential Sound types and Auto-Match (`essentialSound.autoMatch`). The real mix with the mixer and automation after picture lock, or it's redone with every timing change.

context.q: My night street shots are noisy
context.a: Temporal noise reduction on the clip, and keep the blacks deep rather than lifting them.

q: the street lamps make everyone orange
a: If skin is the priority, partly neutralise the sodium-orange with a qualifier.

context.a: A text layer with a box shape behind it, the box pinned to the text (`graphics.pin`) so it grows with the name.

a: Left-aligned text (`graphics.alignTextLeft`) inside the safe margins, about 5–10 % from the frame edges (`graphics.alignFrame.left`, then nudge inwards).

context.q: How do I put B-roll over my interview?
context.a: Target V2 and turn off source audio (`timeline.setTargeting`), then Overwrite (`source.overwrite`); the interview stays on V1 / A1.

q: what kind of B-roll works best?
a: Pictures of what the speaker talks about: the voice carries the story and the pictures illustrate it. Unrelated shots that only decorate feel like filler.
